title: Durable-text lint rules: count-word and relative-time
summary: Adds two deterministic writing-lint rules that guard text which has to stay true after it is written. `count-word` (error) flags a count of things such as "three stages" or "5 checkpoints", and `relative-time` (warning) flags words that point at the moment of reading such as `today`, `now`, `currently` and `still`. Both read the sentence's words rather than a bare character pattern, both are skipped in a chat transcript, and both are excused by a local absolute date, a source link or note, a stated limit, a past-tense event or a fixed fact. The rest of the diff is the prose sweep the new rules forced across the repository's own documents, plus the rule metadata, the rule registration and a measure test with positive and negative fixtures.

nodes.label: osf CLI
nodes.subtitle: lint writing, hook stop, hook prompt
nodes.summary: The command-line entry point. It reads files or standard input, runs the writing lint and prints findings.

nodes.label: hook stop
nodes.subtitle: agent Stop event
nodes.summary: Reads a coding agent's Stop event and lints the final message. It refuses the stop when the message has errors, and also when the message could not be checked at all.

nodes.label: hook prompt
nodes.subtitle: prompt-submitted event
nodes.summary: Prints context for a new turn: a reminder of the writing shapes a model slips into, then any style advice the last stop check stored.

nodes.label: lint_writing
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Splits text into paragraphs and sentences, runs the rule set, then filters findings by context and suppression. It now drops count-word and relative-time findings when the context is a transcript.

nodes.label: per_sentence
nodes.subtitle: rules.rs
nodes.summary: Builds the per-sentence rule list and runs it over the document. It now constructs the count-word and relative-time rules from the whole text and pushes them into the list.

nodes.label: rule_ids
nodes.subtitle: rules.rs
nodes.summary: The list of rule ids the lint knows. It now names count-word and relative-time.

nodes.label: RULE_META
nodes.subtitle: meta.rs
nodes.summary: The documentation block for every rule: what it does, why it is bad, its class, its citation, an example and its coverage. It gained entries for count-word and relative-time, and several existing entries were reworded.

nodes.label: CountWordRule
nodes.subtitle: count-word, Level::Error
nodes.summary: Flags a count of things written in words or digits, such as "three stages" or "5 checkpoints". It reads a number from two upward, then up to two plain words or adverbs, then a plural noun. Bounds, ranges, "a dozen", "both", "a pair of", hyphen compounds and "one" before a list noun are counts too.

nodes.label: RelativeTimeRule
nodes.subtitle: relative-time, Level::Warning
nodes.summary: Flags a word that points at the time of reading, such as `today`, `now`, `currently`, `this week`, `yet` and `still` where it means time. It stays silent where the word is not about time, such as `now that`, `as soon as` or `still images`.

nodes.label: prepare
nodes.subtitle: sentence preparation
nodes.summary: Turns a raw sentence into the text the rules read. A code span becomes the word "code" unless it holds a date or prose, a link keeps its text and loses its address, a bracketed note is remembered as a source, and every absolute date becomes a marker.

nodes.label: tool_blocks
nodes.subtitle: osf:NAME:start head=SHA
nodes.summary: Finds the byte ranges of blocks a tool wrote between osf markers for the names status, tree and pr-lens, when the start marker names a head commit. A count or a time word inside one is a snapshot of that commit, so both rules skip it.

nodes.label: Local exemptions
nodes.subtitle: date, source, limit, past event, fixed fact
nodes.summary: Every exemption covers only the count or the time word it sits with. A date excuses only its own clause. A source excuses only the count it directly backs. A stated limit, a past-tense event and a fixed fact each excuse only their own phrase.

nodes.label: Existing per-sentence rules
nodes.subtitle: filler, chat-local-reference, and the rest
nodes.summary: The rules the new ones sit beside: filler, chat-local-reference, heading-in-short-text, undefined-name, recap-ending and the other per-sentence checks. They are unchanged, but they share the rule list, the context filter and the suppression pass with the new rules.

nodes.label: writing_measure.rs
nodes.subtitle: precision and recall of exactly one
nodes.summary: Reads the positive and negative fixtures, runs each sentence through the lint, and requires precision and recall of exactly one. It also asserts neither rule runs in a transcript, both hold their level in every durable context, and fenced code is left alone.

nodes.label: writing-measure fixtures
nodes.subtitle: count-word and relative-time, positive and negative
nodes.summary: One sentence per line, copied from this repository's own documents wherever one exists. A positive line names the excerpts the rule must report; a negative line must produce nothing.

nodes.label: Repository prose sweep
nodes.subtitle: docs, READMEs, decision records
nodes.summary: The repository's own documents were rewritten where the new rules would fire: counts became "several" or "each", relative times became dates or plain facts, and rule examples were reworded. This is the change the new rules forced on the corpus they run over.

flows.title: A sentence through the count-word rule
flows.summary: One sentence is prepared, tokenised, scanned for a count, and either excused locally or reported as an error.

messages.label: inside a tool block? skip
messages.note: A sentence inside an osf:status, osf:tree or osf:pr-lens block with a head commit is a snapshot, so the rule returns no findings.

messages.label: tokens, clauses, quotes
messages.note: The rule splits the prepared text into whitespace words, clause bounds and quoted spans before looking for a count.

messages.label: excused(hit)?
messages.note: A date in the same clause, a source link or note, a stated limit, a past-tense verb, an estimate or a fixed fact each excuse only the count they sit with.

messages.label: Finding(count-word, Error, excerpt)
messages.note: The finding carries the owner's remediation text: name the things, or say each, every or these.

flows.title: A sentence through the relative-time rule
flows.summary: One sentence is prepared, matched against the time-word pattern, and each match is judged for whether it is about time.

messages.label: inside a tool block? skip
messages.note: The same tool-block skip applies, so a status or tree block written for a head commit is left alone.

messages.label: match the time-word pattern
messages.note: The pattern covers today, now, currently, at the moment, this week, recently, soon, yet and still, among others.

messages.label: date in clause? is_time_sense?
messages.note: A date in the same clause excuses the word. Otherwise the words around it decide whether it is about time, so `now that`, `as soon as` and `still images` pass.

messages.label: Finding(relative-time, Warning, excerpt)
messages.note: The finding carries the remediation: state the date, or state the fact without a time word.
